subject: Memory accumulation in simulation replications despite using RM()

messages.author: e66baf722e0aed3f
messages.subject: Memory accumulation in simulation replications despite using RM()
parts:
I am writing to ask about possible sources of and remedies for memory accumulation issues in RStan.

In my program there are several students currently running simulations to investigate the performance of multilevel models using R and RStan, but students are routinely running into difficulties when running multiple replications: after a handful of replications (2-5), students are encountering errors where there is insufficient memory to allocate vectors, or when models are run using RStudio on AWS instances, the servers crash as a result of insufficient memory.

A common feature of the models that myself and other students are running is the existence of parameters which covary, and the use of multi_normal or multi_normal_cholesky draws within the Stan code. There are several posts on various message boards related to memory accumulation in RStan, but the issue with memory accumulation when running the multi_normal function was said to be addressed in the most recent version of the program (https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/130).

We are currently running RStan Version 2.12.1, packaged: 2016-09-11 13:07:50 UTC, GitRev: 85f7a56811da, and still encountering issues with memory accumulation.

Details from a specific use case (code and original dataset) are contained in this Google Drive link:
​​https://drive.google.com/open?id=0B0iDFf0080xBaXlpNV9Ib1ZWVWs

- Raw data matrices are approximately 300 MB in size.
- Per discussions on Google Groups (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/memory%7Csort:date/stan-users/HpdXNz2iA7E/T-eFvQq9BQAJ) the rm() command was included in the code. No reduction of memory usage wa observed when “rm(fit)” was used before starting the next replication; using “rm(list=ls())” reduced memory accumulation by approximately 50% per replication but doe not address the problem in full.
- Prior to the inclusion of an rm() command, only two replications could be run before the program terminated with the error, “Error: cannot allocate vector of size 935.3 Mb."

Is CmdStan the solution to the accumulation problem? Could a different placement of the rm() command help address memory accumulation? Are the draws from the multinormal distribution likely the issue?

Given that students often run tens or sometimes hundreds of replications per cell in statistical simulations, this problem is one we are eager to solve and would appreciate any insight.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Memory accumulation in simulation replications despite using RM()
parts:
On Saturday, October 15, 2016 at 7:52:41 AM UTC-4, Shauna Sweet wrote:
Is CmdStan the solution to the accumulation problem? Could a different placement of the rm() command help address memory accumulation? Are the draws from the multinormal distribution likely the issue?

The biggest difference between CmdStan and RStan is that CmdStan by default does not save the warmup iterations whereas RStan does. But you can pass save_warmup = FALSE to stan() and it will not save the warmup. Another difference is that if you are using 4 parallel chains in RStan, it holds 4 copies of the data in R and 4 copies in C++ whereas 4 parallel chains in CmdStan will only hold 4 copies of the data in C++.

You can also pass pars = character(0) and sample_file = "my_model" to stan(), in which case it will write everything to the disk like CmdStan does. You can read the resulting csv files (called my_model_1, my_model_2, my_model_3, and my_model_4) into R via read_stan_csv(), but you may still have the problem that you can't load all the draws with the available memory.

Possibly some memory is used by having the DLL loaded into R. You could try executing

dyn.unload(file.path(tempdir(), paste0(get_stanmodel(posterior)@dso@dso_filename, .Platform$dynlib.ext)))

where posterior is an object produced by stan() that you don't need anymore, but do that before calling rm().

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Memory accumulation in simulation replications despite using RM()
parts:
On Sunday, October 16, 2016 at 12:14:27 PM UTC-4, Shauna Sweet wrote:
I will work on the dyn.unload() command; though whenever I try to include save_warmup = FALSE into the stan() command, I get the following: "Error: passing unknown arguments: save_warmup"... Not sure why this is happening?

That was a bug. It works with 2.12.1 if you call stan_model() and then sampling() or it works with stan() if you install rstan from GitHub.

Ben
